reasons: The cited Section 6.3 does contain a counterparty-side (Servicer/Marketing Agent, i.e., Cellco) indemnity running to the Issuer and trustees for willful misconduct, bad faith and gross negligence, with the standard procedural mechanics the rule expects (prompt notice that is not a condition to recovery absent prejudice, counterparty-funded defence with counsel reasonably satisfactory to the Indemnified Person, separate counsel on conflict) and survival — so the walk-away scenario (no counterparty indemnity, or one-way customer indemnity) is not present.

The indemnity is uncapped and there is no reciprocal Issuer/Depositor indemnity for the Servicer's services, so on the material terms the clause is at least as protective as the fallback (which would tolerate a 3x super-cap).

The failed deterministic check for an IP-infringement limb is a context artifact: this is a securitization transfer and servicing agreement with no deliverables, licensed technology or IP grant, so the absent IP limb is a non-material sub-element. The rationale discloses it (and the Depositor's exclusion from 'Indemnified Person') rather than overstating compliance, which is the correct treatment under the playbook's classification semantics.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed; the record is retained as internal evidence and no actionable edit is required.
